text:
From connect for success to connect for a better world 🌍
It was an honor to be in New Delhi last week to launch the Brevo Foundation and the partnership with J-PAL South Asia and Nobel Prize Esther Duflo !
When ties between people weaken, isolation and precarity grow, and health, equal opportunity and civic life suffer. This is why the Brevo Foundation, Brevo’s endowment fund, works on one cause: social connection. It supports associations that create, strengthen or restore real-life bonds between people, through financial grants and the time and skills of Brevonauts.
At Brevo, our mission is to connect for success: optimizing customer relationships. With the Brevo Foundation, we want to act beyond that economic sphere and give more room to connection, dialogue and exchange. By partnering with J-PAL South Asia, we are choosing evidence: identifying, testing and publicizing the approaches that truly strengthen social connection.
At the heart of the partnership: a call for innovations aimed at researcher-NGO pairs, followed by support and evaluations that rigorously measure the effects of the selected initiatives. The program notably includes 3 scoping studies and 1 randomized evaluation, in order to produce evidence on the approaches that strengthen social connection and their effects on living conditions.
This approach is part of the Brevo Foundation’s mission: to act for social connection, at both the individual and societal level. In India, the partnership with J-PAL South Asia also includes a component dedicated to scaling up the Graduation Approach through the Common Minimum Monitoring Framework, in connection with the Indian government program Samaveshi Aajeevika.
Congratulations to the Brevo Foundation team for this launch and to everyone who made this first strategic partnership in India possible !
Let’s connect for a better world
More details on our website https://lnkd.in/edNnmtpa

What can B2B learn from B2C?
We’d like to borrow a few things from the influencer playbook. 👀
ShipBob’s Jeetu Mahtani points out, in B2B, the most influential voices are often customers already using your product.
And they don’t necessarily need a huge following. A customer with 500 or 1,000 followers could help bring in new business if those people trust their recommendation. But how can B2B brands encourage more of that?
Channing Ferrer suggests giving those customers an incentive to spread the word, bringing some of the thinking behind B2C influencer programs into B2B customer advocacy.
Who’s already recommending your product, and what could you do to make it worth their while to keep sharing?

→ What does it need from our data to actually work well?
→ How are we validating the output before we trust it?
→ Where do we still need a human in the loop?
→ Can it learn and improve alongside the business?
In other words, a pretty useful checklist for the next AI pitch that lands on your calendar.
